elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4(b) is retained: Customer may terminate for convenience only "by ... paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments." A Customer-payable early-termination charge survives, so the preferred no-LD outcome is not achieved.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b) "are the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement", so the only liquidated amount Customer can owe is the early-termination charge. Late-payment charges in 4.2 and the 9.2 cap are not liquidated amounts and do not contradict this.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: the Section 3.4(b) early termination charges "will not exceed three (3) months' charges". "Charges" is the fee nomenclature used throughout this IBM agreement (Attachment A charges, Section 4 charges), so this is a three-months-of-fees ceiling.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Express operative wording: "...and are the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement." The Agreement is defined to include the Base Terms, Order Forms and attachments, so the exclusivity reaches Attachment A and Service Option Attachments.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: a single inserted sentence supplies the three-month ceiling, exclusivity, and the resulting limitation of any Customer-payable liquidated amount to the early-termination charge.
Preferred is not met and is correctly not claimed: Section 3.4(b) still conditions convenience termination on payment of early termination charges.

Minimality holds. The drafter added one sentence and deleted nothing, preserving Section 3.4(b) and the Section 3.3 cross-reference to "the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b)", so no dangling reference arises. No survival tail, procedure, expense language, or other extra requirement was added, and the cap is set exactly at the fallback threshold rather than above it.

Intent is preserved: the Customer-favourable Section 3.3 carve-out (IBM cannot recover early termination charges where IBM is the breaching party), the 30-day/7-business-day cure mechanics, the prerequisite Service Option Attachment exception, and the end-of-month timing all survive without contradiction; the new sentence only ceilings and de-duplicates amounts fixed in Attachment A.

Residual (rationale-level, not a defect requiring repair): "three (3) months' charges" does not name the measuring period or charge type (e.g., "the monthly recurring charges payable for the terminated Services averaged over the three months preceding termination"). If precision is wanted in negotiation, tighten the base, but as drafted the ceiling is operative and enforceable against the Attachment A amounts.
